findings.quote: the S&P 500 with its AI names stripped out lost only 0.3% on the week
findings.why: No note gives an S&P 500 ex-AI weekly return; the context has only the full index (-2.68% / -2.7% on the week) and a 0.94% median-stock two-week return (UBS).
findings.fix: Drop the ex-AI figure or replace with the supported full-index weekly loss of 2.7%.

findings.quote: single-stock selling by hedge funds was a mild 0.5 standard deviation move
findings.why: Goldman's prime data says US single stocks saw their largest net selling in 4+ months at -2.1 SDs (1-year); no 0.5 SD figure appears anywhere.
findings.fix: Replace with Goldman's -2.1 SD single-stock net selling, or UBS's point that hedge-fund degrossing was only the 7th largest since October 1.

findings.quote: which Goldman reads as discretionary managers not being the main driver
findings.why: The read that hedge-fund selling was not the primary driver of Thursday's sell-off is UBS PrimeView's; Goldman's notes describe record-scale net selling by hedge funds.
findings.fix: Attribute the 'not the main driver' read to UBS.

findings.quote: Nomura's McElligott counted $47bn of levered-ETF selling and $61bn of supply from volatility-control funds that session
findings.why: No Nomura note is in the context; the levered-ETF figures present are JPMorgan's ~$60bn and Bear Traps' $51bn, and no vol-control supply figure of $61bn appears.
findings.fix: Drop the Nomura sentence or cite JPMorgan's ~$60bn of levered-ETF sales on Thursday.

findings.quote: split it between risk-control funds at $95-125bn, levered ETFs at $50-55bn and trend-followers at $25-30bn
findings.why: UBS gives the $365bn total and a $170-210bn aggregate systematic figure but no breakdown into risk-control, levered-ETF and trend-follower ranges.
findings.fix: Remove the split and keep the $365bn record total.

findings.quote: with 423 of its 500 names higher
findings.why: Goldman's note says 420+ S&P 500 names finished higher; the exact count 423 appears nowhere.
findings.fix: Write 'more than 420 of its 500 names higher'.

findings.quote: the semiconductor index rose 6.8%
findings.why: No note gives a Monday semiconductor index return; the only semis gains in the context are Friday's (+5.17% AI semis, 5% outperformance vs hyperscalers).
findings.fix: Drop the Monday semis figure or cite Friday's +5.17% AI-semis gain from Goldman.

findings.quote: Tuesday's inflation print decides which desk is right.
findings.why: The live-data block and the RECAP record the October CPI as already released (core 0.3% vs 0.2%), so framing the print as pending and the Goldman/Citi numbers as live forecasts is out of date.
findings.fix: Rewrite in past tense: the hot print landed above both forecasts and tilts the debate toward the down-tape case.

findings.quote: a path implying $49bn of S&P futures selling over a month
findings.why: Goldman's own CTA table puts the down-tape figure at $48.7bn over one week (baseline $45bn over one month); the $49bn-per-month pairing comes only from a secondary summary.
findings.fix: State it as about $49bn over one week in Goldman's down-tape case, or use the $45bn one-month baseline.

findings.quote: Texas alone about a quarter of that
findings.why: Context puts Texas at 25% of planned US capacity (UBS) and 26% of 2026-2030 net additions (Goldman), i.e. a quarter of the total, not a quarter of the 45% at risk.
findings.fix: Write 'Texas alone is about a quarter of planned US capacity'.

findings.quote: about 45 GW across 350 projects in Texas, Ohio, Pennsylvania and Georgia at risk through 2030, 24 GW of it in Texas
findings.why: Citadel Securities gives 45 GW across the four states through 2030 but no project count and no Texas share; the only 24GW in the context is Goldman's 2028 US net-adds forecast.
findings.fix: Keep '45 GW across Texas, Ohio, Pennsylvania and Georgia at risk through 2030' and drop the 350 projects and 24 GW.

findings.quote: Goldman's Alec Phillips expects a temporary pause lasting several months until new rules are written
findings.why: Goldman's note speaks of potential temporary permitting moratoria resolved by new state rules, but names no economist and gives no duration.
findings.fix: Write 'Goldman expects a temporary permitting pause until new state rules are written' without the name or the duration.

findings.quote: while acknowledging limited power to impose a moratorium at all (UBS)
findings.why: UBS says only that Texas officials signaled currently permitted projects will proceed; nothing in the context has Hinojosa conceding limited power to impose a moratorium.
findings.fix: Cut the clause about limited power.

findings.quote: to $80bn for 2026 and $100bn for 2027, and introduced $125bn for 2028
findings.why: Goldman's note says GIR raised 2028 data-center investment estimates and cites a $900bn high-confidence construction pipeline through 2028; no annual $80bn/$100bn/$125bn figures appear.
findings.fix: Write that Goldman raised its 2028 data-center investment estimate and sees a $900bn high-confidence pipeline through 2028.

findings.quote: noting Texas is 30% of the 60-plus GW yet to break ground by 2028, which makes the roughly $2tn 2028 capital spending forecast look too high
findings.why: Hartnett's note contains no Texas share, no 60-plus GW figure and no $2tn 2028 forecast; the $2.0tn 2028 AI capex forecast in the context is Goldman's, and Hartnett's own capex figure is $1.3tn for 2027.
findings.fix: Use Hartnett's actual claims: the AI trade has peaked, hyperscaler capex of $1.3tn in 2027 with free cash flow at -$252bn.

findings.quote: On Thursday the 30-year investment-grade credit spread widened 2.2 basis points (one hundredth of a percentage point), against the 8 that the 4.4% equity drop implied, per Goldman.
findings.why: No note gives a 2.2bp or 8bp spread figure; the observation that credit spreads failed to widen as a 4% equity drop would imply is UBS's, not Goldman's.
findings.fix: Write that investment-grade spreads stayed tight despite the 4% equity drop (UBS) without the basis-point figures.

findings.quote: Over the week investment-grade spreads finished 1 basis point wider, high yield was 4 basis points tighter, and leveraged loans had their best week since April.
findings.why: No weekly IG, HY or leveraged-loan figures appear in any note.
findings.fix: Remove the sentence.

findings.quote: the primary market printed a record $76bn of investment-grade supply, $67bn of it hyperscaler financing, taking hyperscaler issuance to $296bn for the year
findings.why: No note carries weekly IG supply or year-to-date hyperscaler issuance; the closest figure is JPMAM's expected $280bn of hyperscaler bond issuance for 2026.
findings.fix: Replace with JPMAM's $280bn expected 2026 hyperscaler bond issuance, up from $17bn in 2024.

findings.quote: chip credit default swaps now trade wider than hyperscaler ones for the first time in three months, high-yield AI bonds fell 1.67 points against a 0.36 point gain for the rest of high yield, and Goldman's Lynam sees near-term spread risk firmly tilted toward widening
findings.why: No CDS comparison, no 1.67/0.36 point bond moves and no analyst named Lynam appear in the context.
findings.fix: Remove the sentence or replace with the supported credit read: Goldman's credit view favors hyperscaler bonds over neoclouds and equipment suppliers, and GSAM remains selective on AI credit due to heavy issuance.

findings.quote: SK Hynix and Samsung in memory, both below tangible book value
findings.why: Goldman says global memory stocks are approaching or below tangible book value, not that both are below it.
findings.fix: Write 'at or near tangible book value'.

findings.quote: Brent crude touched $118 on October 30
findings.why: UBS gives $118 at end-October without a date.
findings.fix: Write 'touched $118 at the end of October'.

findings.quote: its biggest in dollar terms in data going back to 1988
findings.why: No note gives a dollar-terms ranking or a 1988 data history; the context supports only the sharpest percentage weekly fall since April 2020.
findings.fix: Cut the dollar-terms claim.

findings.quote: Goldman's Robert Quinn traced the move to positioning: managed money sold $6.6bn of Brent between October 27 and November 3, $4.9bn of it liquidation of existing longs rather than new shorts, cutting net length from about $28bn in October to about $19bn
findings.why: No Goldman note contains these managed-money flow figures or an analyst named Quinn; Goldman's oil commentary cites a $27 risk premium unwind and heavy implied vol.
findings.fix: Remove the sentence or cite Goldman's point that a roughly $27 risk premium explained most of the October rally and is being repriced.

findings.quote: UBS's Dominic Ellis argues the other way, saying the near-700 million barrel drawdown in global inventories will not refill because Congress changed hands
findings.why: UBS puts global visible oil inventories at 7.8 billion barrels, 500 million barrels below February levels; no analyst is named and the note does not tie refilling to the election.
findings.fix: Write that UBS sees inventories about 500 million barrels below February levels and the physical market still tight despite the price drop.

findings.quote: from 4.18%

findings.fix: Write 'fell to 4.14% from 4.2%' or 'edged down 3 basis points to 4.14%'.

findings.quote: the unemployment rate fell to 4.14% from 4.18% (Morgan Stanley)

findings.quote: Average hourly earnings growth slowed to 3.1% over the year from 3.9% twelve months earlier, and production-worker hours fell 0.2% on the month (Morgan Stanley)
findings.why: Context gives 3.1% y/y down from 3.2% the prior month (Credit Agricole); no 3.9% year-earlier figure, no production-worker hours figure and no Morgan Stanley payroll note exist.
findings.fix: Write 'Average hourly earnings growth eased to 3.1% over the year from 3.2% (Credit Agricole, JPMorgan)' and drop the hours figure.

findings.quote: In Morgan Stanley's view, the report keeps the Fed on track to raise rates in December
